name: deeper-head
hypothesis: Dense(128, relu) hidden layer before output learns nonlinear combinations of YAMNet embeddings, improving buzz sensitivity

baseline.note: different dataset (standard vs lite) — not a clean comparison

conclusion: MLP head worse than linear probe; confounded by lite vs standard set — see deeper-std for clean comparison

name: deeper-std
hypothesis: Adding Dense(128, relu) before output improves over linear probe when trained on standard (not lite) set
conclusion: MLP head is worse than linear probe at high-precision operating point on standard set; linear probing outperforms on YAMNet embeddings

name: combined-embedder
hypothesis: Validate on all classes instead of buzz-only so early stopping calibrates against full precision/recall distribution
conclusion: Marginal improvement at high-precision point (+0.4pp at 95% precision); principled default but not a major lever

name: focal-loss
hypothesis: Focal loss (gamma=2, alpha=0.25) improves sensitivity at 95% precision by downweighting easy negatives
conclusion: Primary metric essentially unchanged; alpha=0.25 penalizes buzz too aggressively — retry with alpha=0.5–0.75

name: focal-loss-alpha
hypothesis: Focal loss with alpha=0.75 corrects over-penalization of buzz in alpha=0.25 experiment
conclusion: Focal loss shifts operating point rather than lifting PR curve; dead end for 95% precision metric

name: label-smooth
hypothesis: Label smoothing (eps=0.1) improves score calibration, lifting sensitivity at 95% precision
conclusion: Best result so far: +2.2pp at 95% precision (0.2763 vs 0.2545); 0.4pp below production target (0.28); try eps=0.05 or LR reduction to close gap

name: label-smooth-02
hypothesis: Label smoothing eps=0.2 closes remaining gap to 0.28 production target
conclusion: Exceeds 0.28 target; monotonic trend — eps=0.3 likely improves further

name: label-smooth-03
hypothesis: Label smoothing eps=0.3 continues monotonic improvement trend from eps=0.1->0.2
conclusion: Catastrophic degradation: eps=0.3 collapses signal; eps=0.2 is confirmed optimal

name: binary-translation
hypothesis: Collapsing all non-buzz classes into single background class focuses linear probe on buzz/background boundary
conclusion: Binary translation hurts; multi-class auxiliary supervision helps

name: dropout-probe
hypothesis: Dropout(0.2) on embeddings before linear probe regularizes overfitting
conclusion: INVALIDATED — stale dataset (pre-3cfb52e); see dropout-repro for replication on current set (0.172)

name: hyperparam-sweep
hypothesis: Sequential sweeps of dropout (0.0-0.4), label smoothing (0.1-0.25), and LR (0.001-0.003) to tune the linear probe under the current combined config
conclusion: 0.295 best is a single lucky run (dropout=0.4); dropout=0.2 gave 0.203 in same sweep; typical range ~0.17–0.25; lr=0.001 reliably bad; variance too high for single-run conclusions

name: dropout-repro
hypothesis: Replicate dropout-probe on current medium set to validate 0.3175 claim
conclusion: 0.3175 was dataset artifact; 0.172 on current set; variance confirmed very high

name: ls02-repro
hypothesis: Replicate label-smooth-02 (no dropout, ls=0.2) on current dataset to establish clean baseline
conclusion: All null-commit results invalid; typical range on current set ~0.16–0.25; single-run estimates unreliable; need multi-run averaging or fixed seeds before drawing conclusions

name: low-delta
hypothesis: min_delta=0.002 prevents premature early stopping on bad initializations, reducing training variance
conclusion: No mean improvement (MW p=0.48) but 6.6x variance reduction (F p=0.023); eliminates failed runs; adopted as default with patience=50, epochs=400

name: buzz-upweight
hypothesis: 2x buzz class weight on top of balanced weighting pushes model toward higher buzz recall without sacrificing precision
conclusion: Negative result: upweighting hurts or is neutral (MW p=0.171, CIs barely overlap). Balanced class weights are already appropriate; bottleneck is not training emphasis on buzz.

name: batchnorm
hypothesis: BatchNormalization of input embeddings before linear probe stabilizes distribution, improving decision boundaries
conclusion: Clear negative: mean drops 5.8pp, CIs don't overlap. BN running stats from training embeddings don't transfer to test-set distribution. Dead end.

name: with-dropout
hypothesis: Dropout(0.2) with standard weights, isolating dropout effect from buzz-upweight confound
conclusion: Dropout neutral: CIs overlap heavily (0.216-0.241 vs 0.207-0.242). Not a lever. Current defaults are stable.

name: temporal-context
hypothesis: Concatenating [prev, curr, next] YAMNet frames (3072-d) lets linear probe detect temporal persistence of buzz vs transient confusable sounds
conclusion: Negative: mean drops 2pp (CI [0.194,0.224] vs [0.216,0.241]). 3x wider input space with same buzz data may simply be harder for the linear probe to fit. Window size (2.88s) may also dilute the buzz signal. Root cause unclear.

name: buzz-in-train
hypothesis: Force all buzz samples from validate into training; early stopping uses non-buzz val classes as proxy
conclusion: Negative: mean drops 2.5pp, variance increases. Early stopping without buzz in val is poorly calibrated for the target class.

name: mlp-head-repro
hypothesis: Dense(128,relu) hidden layer before output may improve over linear probe with current stable methodology (low-delta, 5 runs, ls=0.2)
conclusion: Negative: drops 2.8pp, CIs don't overlap. No overfitting — train/val loss coupled throughout. Hidden layer adds no generalizable structure; linear probe is the better inductive bias for YAMNet embeddings. Architecture complexity is a dead end.

name: supp-freq
hypothesis: Concatenate 4 frequency features (dominant freq, spectral centroid, ZCR, buzz-band energy 100-600Hz) to YAMNet 1024-d embedding
conclusion: Marginal +1.2pp, CIs overlap. Slight directional signal but not a clear win.

name: l2-regularize
hypothesis: L2(1e-4) kernel regularization on Dense probe shrinks spurious embedding dimensions, improving generalization
conclusion: Negative: mean drops 1pp, lower CI bound regresses substantially. Dropout + label smoothing already sufficient regularization; explicit weight decay over-regularizes.

name: no-reg-baseline
hypothesis: Establish zero-regularization reference: linear probe with no dropout, no label smoothing, no L2
conclusion: True zero-regularization baseline: 0.193, 3.6pp below current defaults. Dropout+LS together account for the full gap. Very low variance (std=0.010).

name: l2-only
hypothesis: L2(1e-4) as sole regularizer (no dropout, no label smoothing) isolates L2 contribution vs true baseline
conclusion: L2 alone is identical to no regularization (CIs fully overlap). Dropout+LS are responsible for all gains in current defaults. L2 is a dead end.

name: yamnet-ft
hypothesis: Fine-tune YAMNet layers 13-14 with LR=1e-5 after warming up the head; two-phase training
conclusion: Clear negative (-8.3pp). Backbone overfits despite LR=1e-5; train acc ~78% vs val ~59%. Dataset too small for backbone adaptation. Dead end.

name: supp-freq-v2
hypothesis: Buzz-band-specific features (spectral flatness and centroid within 100-600 Hz) are more discriminative than global features used in supp-freq; tested on no-reg-baseline config to isolate feature contribution
conclusion: Neutral: CIs fully overlap. YAMNet already encodes relevant frequency structure; handcrafted frequency features are a dead end.
